newsitem.title: ITALY: Italy's Confindustria urges interest rate cut.
newsitem.headline: Italy's Confindustria urges interest rate cut.

text.p: Giorgio Fossa, the head of Italian industraliasts' confederation Confindustria, on Friday urged the Bank of Italy to lower its official interest rates.
Fossa said that although interest rates had come down over the past year, the cost of money for private borrowers had actually increased since "inflation has gone down faster than interest rates."
"With inflation taken out, the cost of money is much higher now than it was one year ago," Fossa said in a speech to business leaders in the Adriatic city of Ancona.
"We strongly urge (Bank of Italy governor Antonio Fazio) to lower official interest rates," he added.
Fossa said Fazio was being excessively prudent in waiting to make a move.

"By the time he gets around to lowering the rates, the Italian markets could already have been hit by a wave of higher interest rates which is unfortunately developing in other parts of the world," Fossa said.

Many analysts believe Fazio is awaiting details of the government's three-year economic programme, due out later this month, and the outcome of French elections before moving to lower Italian official interest rates.

A fall in official rates triggers lower bank rates, thus helping industry, and allows the government to reduce the costs of servicing Italy's huge public debt, improving its chances of cutting the public deficit.
Italian interest rates have fallen by three percentage points over the last year. -- Rome newsroom +396 678 2505
